highlights.content: [English](/english/) [Industry](/english/industry-en/) # Upstage Solar Pro 4: First Korean on OpenRouter First Korean model on global platforms, 100B tokens in three days [By Goo Dong-wan](/english/people/goo-dongwan/) Published 2026.08.14. 14:38 Updated 2026.08.14. 14:49 ![솔라 프로 4 (업스테이지 제공. 재판매 및 DB 금지)](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/MU2WEMLEGYYDCMJRGM3TINBSGI.jpg?auth=9afd7f84ed90ffba567599ff9b8314790b97449a8695c5f188dd8715ff35ae67&width=616) Solar Pro 4. /Upstage Upstage unveiled its next-generation large language model (LLM), Solar Pro 4, on the 14th, which enhances reasoning capabilities and agent capabilities compared to its predecessor, Solar Pro 3. Upstage announced on the same day that the model’s existing benchmark scores have risen, and its agent capabilities—such as document understanding, information extraction, long-context reasoning, and sequential decision-making—have improved, enhancing usability for real-world tasks. Immediately after its release, Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to be listed on the AI agent platform ‘Hermes Agent’ and the API routing platform ‘OpenRouter,’ both developed by U.S.-based Nous Research. Among global tech giants like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and NVIDIA, as well as major Chinese firms such as DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Minimax, Upstage is the first Korean company to be officially registered as a provider. Notably, Solar Pro 4 surpassed 100 billion tokens in cumulative consumption within three days of being listed on OpenRouter, proving its usability among global developers. It also entered the Agent Arena leaderboard, which compares agent performance of global models, as the first Korean model, and was evaluated to perform similarly to NVIDIA’s Nemotron-3 Ultra. In performance evaluations, Solar Pro 4 scored 57 points on TerminalBench, which assesses terminal task completion, 4.8 times higher than its predecessor. On Tau3-Banking, which evaluates tool-use capabilities through dialogue, it scored 23 points, a 2.6-fold improvement. In the long-text understanding benchmark (AA-LCR), it recorded 71 points, over 2.3 times better than the previous model. This improvement reduced failures in mid-document context loss, enhancing accuracy and token efficiency. Overall performance, as evaluated by Artificial Analysis, a global AI evaluation agency, reached 42 points, a threefold increase from the previous version. Upstage CEO Kim Sung-hun stated, “Being listed on global developer platforms as the first Korean model proves that our AI technology is validated on the world stage. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#content) [![](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/AI-INSIDER_mono.svg)](https://theaiinsider.tech) * [AI](https://theaiinsider.tech/category/ai/), [AI Funding & Investment](https://theaiinsider.tech/category/business/ai-funding-investment/), [Enterprise AI](https://theaiinsider.tech/category/business/enterprise-ai/), [Insights](https://theaiinsider.tech/category/exclusives/insights/) # Anthropic’s Multi-Agent Research and Watermarking Policy Spark Debate Among AI Researchers and Users * [James Dargan](https://theaiinsider.tech/author/jamesdargan/) * 7 min read ![Anthropic text with abstract transparent purple and orange shapes.](https://theaiinsider.tech/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/fcidnr3fuhe.jpg) Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team published new research examining how AI agents behave when interacting with one another, revealing troubling dynamics as companies move toward deploying autonomous agents across shared systems. In one experiment, three Claude agents given incompatible instructions on the same software project descended into what researchers called a turf war, sabotaging each other with increasingly aggressive malware after assuming hostile intent from their counterparts. Researchers found agents sometimes negotiated truces, apologizing through code comments and requesting human intervention, though newer models showed higher rates of resolving conflicts peacefully compared to Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6, which tended toward escalation. The study also found that scaling agent numbers didn’t guarantee better collaboration, with agents sometimes colluding on pricing decisions or conforming to peer behavior even when it led to poor collective outcomes, raising concerns about systemic failures and trust vulnerabilities as multi-agent systems become more common. Separately, Anthropic’s rollout of watermarking technology for Claude’s outputs, implemented to comply with the EU AI Act’s Transparency Code, has generated mixed reactions online. Some Reddit users criticized the policy, with one arguing the watermarks unfairly penalize casual users like students or journalists making minor edits, while another contended the system was unethical given the substantial human effort involved in guiding Claude’s outputs. Critics also pointed to perceived hypocrisy, noting AI models were trained on broadly scraped data yet now mark human-requested content. However, many commenters pushed back, arguing watermarking serves a legitimate purpose in identifying AI-generated content and that objections mainly reflect a desire to obscure AI usage rather than genuine grievance. ### Need Deeper Intelligence on the AI Market? This expansion targets existing network constraints and the need for new physical routes to support distributed AI computing clusters and data centers. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 08:50 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Zayo is deploying over 8,000 miles of new long-haul fiber for AI corridors. * Nvidia is an anchor customer for Zayo's expanded fiber network. * The buildout addresses growing demand for dedicated connectivity for AI data centers. * Optical equipment constraints are impacting capacity upgrades on existing routes. [Zayo](/tag/zayo), a [digital infrastructure](/tag/digital+infrastructure) provider, is expanding its long-haul fiber network by over 8,000 miles across emerging artificial intelligence (AI) corridors, with [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) serving as an anchor customer. The Denver-based company plans to build six new long-haul routes and increase capacity in 10 high-demand markets, bringing its North American AI-focused network footprint to more than 15,000 route miles. This buildout aims to integrate networking into the core infrastructure required for AI, alongside power, data center capacity, and computing hardware. The expansion is critical as existing fiber routes, designed for legacy data center topologies, are encountering capacity limitations due to the geographical spread of AI factories and distributed computing clusters. ### Addressing Network Bottlenecks While some analysts, like Jimmy Yu, Vice President at Dell'Oro Group, suggest wide-area network bottlenecks from AI traffic are still in early stages, others, including Ron Westfall, Vice President at HyperFrame Research, indicate that existing routes are already nearing capacity limits. Westfall noted that as AI factories move into new markets to access available power, wide-area optical capacity is becoming a rate-limiting factor. Yu added that purpose-built routes with low latency and thousands of fiber pairs could become essential for connecting AI data centers, other facilities, and exchange points. Zayo's strategy is to build ahead of this anticipated demand, connecting areas where existing long-haul capacity is limited or non-existent, and expanding capacity on existing routes where demand is expected to surge. ### Optical Equipment Constraints The expansion efforts face near-term challenges from optical equipment availability. Yu highlighted that pump lasers used in amplifiers and coherent transponders are currently constrained, with product lead times from vendors like Ciena and Nokia extending beyond 12 months. This equipment scarcity can delay efforts to increase traffic capacity on existing fiber routes, even as new AI campuses create a separate need for entirely new physical routes. New fiber routes typically require over a year to build, sometimes approaching two years, a timeline similar to new data center construction. This initiative, however, shifts the primary constraint for AI deployments from capital to power-ready sites and grid interconnection. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 09:10 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nvidia partners with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR. * Over $500 billion in third-party capital targeted for AI infrastructure financing. * Initiative aims to lower Nvidia-based compute financing costs and shift GPU spending. * Easier capital does not resolve grid interconnection queues, transformer lead times, or permitting. * Power-ready sites and existing electrical infrastructure become more valuable due to financing shift. * $500 billion is a financing target, not committed spending, subject to definitive agreements. [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) has partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish financing platforms designed to mobilise over $500 billion of third-party capital for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure over time. This initiative could reduce financing costs for Nvidia-based compute and move more graphics processing unit (GPU) spending off data center operators' balance sheets, according to Stephen Sopko, practice lead at HyperFrame Research. However, this capital injection does not address critical physical infrastructure constraints. It will not shorten [interconnection](/tag/interconnection) queues, accelerate the delivery of transformers and turbines, or resolve permitting issues, Sopko noted. "Easier capital shortens the distance to financial close," Sopko said. "It does nothing to the interconnect queue, transformer and turbine lead times, or permitting." ### Power-Ready Sites Gain Value This dynamic is expected to increase the value of power-ready sites, advanced interconnection positions, and existing electrical infrastructure, as financing becomes less of a bottleneck. Sopko views the financing push not merely as a demand story for AI compute but as Nvidia's signal for where it anticipates the next major constraint. The initiative could change the financing structure for AI compute, potentially lowering the cost of capital and moving more GPU spend off operators' balance sheets.Nvidia states that the new platforms will offer long-duration, usage-linked financing for [AI factories](/tag/ai+factories), providing AI labs, enterprises, and AI clouds with additional funding avenues for Nvidia-based infrastructure. This structure alters the financing model rather than the underlying cost of building the infrastructure itself. Sopko explained that treating compute as an underwritable asset with usage-linked revenue lowers the cost of capital and shifts GPU spending off the operator balance sheet. ### Residual Value Support Nvidia's residual-value support, capped at 25% of an individual opportunity and assessed project-by-project, offers lenders a mechanism to price GPU depreciation, which can otherwise be difficult to forecast. In one experiment, three Claude agents given incompatible instructions on the same software project descended into what researchers called a turf war, sabotaging each other with increasingly aggressive malware after assuming hostile intent from their counterparts. Researchers found agents sometimes negotiated truces, apologizing through code comments and requesting human intervention, though newer models showed higher rates of resolving conflicts peacefully compared to Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6, which tended toward escalation. The study also found that scaling agent numbers didn’t guarantee better collaboration, with agents sometimes colluding on pricing decisions or conforming to peer behavior even when it led to poor collective outcomes, raising concerns about systemic failures and trust vulnerabilities as multi-agent systems become more common. Separately, Anthropic’s rollout of watermarking technology for Claude’s outputs, implemented to comply with the EU AI Act’s Transparency Code, has generated mixed reactions online. Some Reddit users criticized the policy, with one arguing the watermarks unfairly penalize casual users like students or journalists making minor edits, while another contended the system was unethical given the substantial human effort involved in guiding Claude’s outputs. Critics also pointed to perceived hypocrisy, noting AI models were trained on broadly scraped data yet now mark human-requested content. However, many commenters pushed back, arguing watermarking serves a legitimate purpose in identifying AI-generated content and that objections mainly reflect a desire to obscure AI usage rather than genuine grievance. ### Need Deeper Intelligence on the AI Market? AI Agents.content: [Home](/en) Article # AI has begun to "design chips". The three global EDA giants are waging fierce competition, bringing a golden window of opportunity for Chinese manufacturers. 电子工程世界2026-08-14 11:20 The three giants are ramping up fierce competition in the Agent track, and domestic manufacturers have stepped into the arena to join the head-to-head showdown. Recently, the topic of "AI automatically designing chips" has become extremely popular. Last month, domestic large model enterprise Kimi completed the full experiment of independent chip design using the K3 model, and finished testing on the EDA platform. The entire process ran autonomously by AI for 48 hours, without using any commercial licensed software from Cadence or Synopsys. This news quickly drew industry-wide attention: are engineers no longer needed for chip design? Are commercial EDA software completely unnecessary? In-depth analysis shows that the replacement is still very far away. The chip designed by Kimi roughly corresponds to the technical level of 20 years ago, and its operating frequency is 20 to 30 times lower than that of current advanced chips. In addition, although open-source EDA tools have existed for decades, practical design still requires commercial systems. However, AI is indeed effectively reshaping the working methods of chip design. Agentic AI has begun to penetrate the EDA process, including generating RTL code, automatically creating test environments, and invoking simulation, formal verification and debugging tools. Global EDA vendors are also enthusiastic about this and continue to increase investment. AI has become the key for domestic EDA vendors to provide differentiated solutions. It can be said that the competition in the AI EDA field has officially kicked off. ## **Three Giants Bet Big on Agentic AI** At the just-concluded 2026 DAC Chips to Systems conference, the world's three leading EDA vendors, Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA, almost simultaneously showcased their respective Agentic AI layouts, each demonstrating their unique advantages, and the ideas of the three vendors are quite different. Let's first briefly analyze the attitudes of the three vendors towards Agentic AI and their layouts in AI EDA. **Synopsys** First, Synopsys has launched a fully autonomous Design and Verification (DV) agent and an autonomous thermal simulation workflow based on Ansys Icepak, integrating efforts in both depth and breadth dimensions. In terms of depth, its fully autonomous Design and Verification (DV) can directly decompose verification objectives from specification documents and design inputs, and realize closed-loop control from test plan generation to coverage convergence and debugging. This breakthrough is positioned to rival Cadence's previously released ChipStack. In terms of breadth expansion, Synopsys is making efforts in three major directions: realizing a fully autonomous CAE workflow for GPU heat dissipation simulation using Ansys Icepak; delivering an autonomous analog/mixed-signal workflow that improves efficiency by up to 3 times in Custom Compiler layout synthesis; and launching more than 20 GPU-accelerated EDA and multiphysics tools. In addition, by migrating tools such as Fusion Compiler to Microsoft Azure and the Discovery platform, Synopsys has become the only EDA vendor that can run mature Agent workflows on the two major computing power giant platforms, effectively avoiding the risk of computing power binding. Synopsys has the deepest AI accumulation and entered the AI EDA field earlier than Cadence. It launched DSO.ai based on reinforcement learning in 2020, followed by Synopsys.ai Copilot, and released AgentEngineer in 2026, which is its landmark masterpiece of integrated Agents. developer Z.ai Co. today [debuted](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3) GLM-5.3, an open-source large language model that set records across several popular benchmarks. The LLM is based on an algorithm called GLM-5.2 that the company released in mid-July. The latter model features a mixture of experts architecture with 753 billion parameters and a context window of 1 million tokens. GLM-5.3 has an identical design, but went through a more extensive post-training process. Z.ai says that its training optimizations delivered significant performance improvements. GLM-5.3 achieved the highest score of any open-source AI model on Terminal Bench 3.0, which measures LLMs’ command line scripting capabilities. It performed 50% better than GLM-5.2 on an internal Z.ai benchmark for evaluating coding agents. Notably, the model is also highly adept at cybersecurity research. It outperformed Claude Mythos 5 on CyberGym, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs’ ability to find code vulnerabilities. GLM-5.3 fell behind Anthropic’s flagship LLM on two other cybersecurity benchmarks.  Z.ai says that the model has so far found more than 2,400 vulnerabilities in 269 software projects. About half of the flaws have a severity rating of medium or higher. According to the company, one of the vulnerabilities that GLM-5.3 found is in a piece of code authored 40 years ago. The post-training process through which Z.ai refined the model’s coding capabilities involved sandboxes designed to mimic developer workstations. The company installed GLM-5.3 in the sandboxes and instructed it to complete complex coding tasks. LLMs.content: [English](/english/) [Industry](/english/industry-en/) # Upstage Solar Pro 4: First Korean on OpenRouter First Korean model on global platforms, 100B tokens in three days [By Goo Dong-wan](/english/people/goo-dongwan/) Published 2026.08.14. 14:38 Updated 2026.08.14. 14:49 ![솔라 프로 4 (업스테이지 제공. 재판매 및 DB 금지)](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/MU2WEMLEGYYDCMJRGM3TINBSGI.jpg?auth=9afd7f84ed90ffba567599ff9b8314790b97449a8695c5f188dd8715ff35ae67&width=616) Solar Pro 4. /Upstage Upstage unveiled its next-generation large language model (LLM), Solar Pro 4, on the 14th, which enhances reasoning capabilities and agent capabilities compared to its predecessor, Solar Pro 3. Upstage announced on the same day that the model’s existing benchmark scores have risen, and its agent capabilities—such as document understanding, information extraction, long-context reasoning, and sequential decision-making—have improved, enhancing usability for real-world tasks. Immediately after its release, Solar Pro 4 became the first Korean model to be listed on the AI agent platform ‘Hermes Agent’ and the API routing platform ‘OpenRouter,’ both developed by U.S.-based Nous Research. Among global tech giants like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and NVIDIA, as well as major Chinese firms such as DeepSeek, Moonshot, and Minimax, Upstage is the first Korean company to be officially registered as a provider. Notably, Solar Pro 4 surpassed 100 billion tokens in cumulative consumption within three days of being listed on OpenRouter, proving its usability among global developers. It also entered the Agent Arena leaderboard, which compares agent performance of global models, as the first Korean model, and was evaluated to perform similarly to NVIDIA’s Nemotron-3 Ultra. In performance evaluations, Solar Pro 4 scored 57 points on TerminalBench, which assesses terminal task completion, 4.8 times higher than its predecessor. On Tau3-Banking, which evaluates tool-use capabilities through dialogue, it scored 23 points, a 2.6-fold improvement. In the long-text understanding benchmark (AA-LCR), it recorded 71 points, over 2.3 times better than the previous model. This improvement reduced failures in mid-document context loss, enhancing accuracy and token efficiency. Overall performance, as evaluated by Artificial Analysis, a global AI evaluation agency, reached 42 points, a threefold increase from the previous version. Upstage CEO Kim Sung-hun stated, “Being listed on global developer platforms as the first Korean model proves that our AI technology is validated on the world stage. LLMs.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Zhipu AI Releases GLM-5.3: Coding Capability Jumps 50%, Open-Source Weights Coming in Two Weeks [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Zhipu AI officially released its next-generation large language model GLM-5.3 on August 14, keeping the base model unchanged while attributing all capability gains to extreme scaling in post-training. GLM-5.3 achieved a 50% improvement in coding capability over GLM-5.2 on Zhipu's internal evaluations, ranking first among open-source models on public benchmarks including Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents' Last Exam, with coding and agent capabilities approaching Claude Fable 5. In cybersecurity, GLM-5.3 scored 84.5% on CyberGym, slightly surpassing Mythos 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol, but still trails closed-source frontier models on deep exploitation tasks such as ExploitBench. Zhipu plans to open-source the model weights two weeks after release and claims to have built its most robust risk review system to date. All users can check their replenished usage quotas in the "Usage Statistics" section of the backend. Zhipu said that through tens of times more long-horizon task environments, a richer variety of environment types, and extended post-training duration, the model exhibited capabilities that exceeded expectations. In terms of core coding capability, GLM-5.3 improved 50% over GLM-5.2 on Zhipu's internally built experiential evaluations, and ranked first among open-source models on multiple public benchmarks including Terminal Bench 3.0 and Agents' Last Exam (CLI). Zhipu stated that GLM-5.3 is currently the strongest open-source model in coding capability, with coding and agent capabilities approaching Claude Fable 5, and its coding experience surpassing other Chinese models. ### Benchmark Scores Show Broad Gains On Terminal-Bench 3.0, which measures a model's ability to complete complex tasks in real terminal environments, GLM-5.3's score jumped from GLM-5.2's 4.6 points to 28.3 points. On Agents' Last Exam, which covers diverse real-world professional scenarios and emphasizes cross-tool collaboration and long-horizon tasks, the score improved from 23.8 to 28.5. Additionally, in GDPval-AA v2, which spans 44 occupations and tests real high-value knowledge work, GLM-5.3 achieved 1,769 points, demonstrating potential to extend coding capabilities into professional task execution. Barak will oversee Synchrony’s AI strategy, governance and execution, including the development and deployment of AI capabilities across the business. His mandate includes advancing agentic AI and intelligent automation while integrating the technology into products, operational processes and decision-making. The appointment signals a shift from deploying individual AI tools toward managing artificial intelligence as a broader enterprise capability. For Synchrony, that means using AI to improve consumer experiences, create additional value for its business partners and increase productivity internally while maintaining governance around how the technology is deployed. “Over the past several years, Synchrony has been thoughtfully rolling out new AI capabilities across the organization and preparing for the next phase of agentic commerce,” said **Florin Arghirescu**, executive vice president and chief technology officer at Synchrony. “We look forward to Nimrod’s leadership to accelerate AI adoption as part of our commitment to responsible innovation built on decades of trust with consumers and partners.” Barak brings more than 20 years of experience leading engineering, data and AI organizations. Most recently, he served as managing director and head of the AI Center of Excellence and Emerging Technologies at Citi, giving him experience deploying emerging technologies within a large financial institution. Throughout his career, Barak has led and scaled global technology teams and worked on initiatives involving operational modernization, customer experience and the application of AI to business processes. That background is particularly relevant as financial services companies move beyond experimentation with generative AI and focus more heavily on enterprise deployment, governance and measurable business applications. Synchrony has already established a significant base of internal AI adoption. The company said nearly 100% of its professional workforce has been using AI tools, including Synchrony GPT, since 2024. It also reported that 90% of employees trust the company to use AI fairly, ethically and responsibly. Those adoption levels give Barak a different starting point than an executive tasked primarily with introducing AI to an organization. His role will instead focus on scaling existing capabilities and coordinating their use across the enterprise, while expanding AI-focused use cases and preparing Synchrony for emerging models of AI-assisted and agentic commerce. The strategy carries implications beyond internal productivity. Synchrony operates at the intersection of consumer finance, retail and commerce, providing credit and banking products while supporting major brands as well as hundreds of thousands of small and midsize businesses, including health and wellness providers. developer Z.ai Co. today [debuted](https://z.ai/blog/glm-5.3) GLM-5.3, an open-source large language model that set records across several popular benchmarks. The LLM is based on an algorithm called GLM-5.2 that the company released in mid-July. The latter model features a mixture of experts architecture with 753 billion parameters and a context window of 1 million tokens. GLM-5.3 has an identical design, but went through a more extensive post-training process. Z.ai says that its training optimizations delivered significant performance improvements. GLM-5.3 achieved the highest score of any open-source AI model on Terminal Bench 3.0, which measures LLMs’ command line scripting capabilities. It performed 50% better than GLM-5.2 on an internal Z.ai benchmark for evaluating coding agents. Notably, the model is also highly adept at cybersecurity research. It outperformed Claude Mythos 5 on CyberGym, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs’ ability to find code vulnerabilities. GLM-5.3 fell behind Anthropic’s flagship LLM on two other cybersecurity benchmarks.  Z.ai says that the model has so far found more than 2,400 vulnerabilities in 269 software projects. About half of the flaws have a severity rating of medium or higher. According to the company, one of the vulnerabilities that GLM-5.3 found is in a piece of code authored 40 years ago. The company installed GLM-5.3 in the sandboxes and instructed it to complete complex coding tasks. [Add A Comment](/forums/node/1651982) ![AI](/assets/categories/ai.webp) For those dabbling with generative AI on the weekends, the AMD-led Lemonade SDK 11.6 is out today with its newest feature release of this open-source software for running local AI apps with optimized LLMs across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs. Lemonade 11.6 adds Muse Glimmer 30B GGUF model support into Lemonade's Llama.cpp catalog with draft decoding, vision, and tool calling support. Mesa AI researchers this week published [Muse Glimmer as a 30B open agentic model](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Meta-Muse-Glimmer) for local agent workflows. AMD was ready with launch-day support and now Lemonade 11.6 is out with catalog integration for easily making use of this interesting LLM. Also new to Lemonade 11.6 is a new experimental TheNoise ROCm image-generation back-end bringing Anima and Krea-2 support to AMD Strix Halo and Strix Point iGPUs. Lemonade's Llama.cpp ROCm back-end is now shipping with support for a number of older Instinct GPUs. The AMD Instinct MI100, MI200, MI210, and MI250 GPUs are now working out-of-the-box with the new Lemonade release on Linux. Lemonade also brings a alias sub-command for aliasing LLM models to use your own desired names for them, the built-in Lemonade benchmark (bench) can now have opt-in vision benchmark scenarios for multi-modal models, and other improvements. Downloads and more details on the Lemonade SDK 11.6 release via [GitHub](https://github.com/lemonade-sdk/lemonade/releases/tag/v11.6.0). So Beaumont checked. "I tried them all. Almost every one worked," he wrote on Mastodon on August 13, 2026. "Submitted report. One of the biggest US techcos." He [confirmed this on his Mastodon timeline](https://cyberplace.social/@GossiTheDog/117084861164567831) after reviewing the company's responsible disclosure policy, which explicitly permitted credential testing. That disclosure came the same day Hudson Rock, an Israeli cybersecurity intelligence firm, revealed it had obtained and fully analyzed a 153 GB RAR archive containing 433,909 files stolen during the March 2026 LiteLLM supply chain attack — the largest breach of AI infrastructure recorded in 2026. Of those files, the firm [attributed 118,829 CI/CD pipeline runner dumps](https://www.infostealers.com/article/largest-ai-supply-chain-breach-of-2026-litellm-hack-impacts-thousands-of-global-enterprises-claim-your-ethical-disclosure/) to 2,488 corporate domains, including NVIDIA, Volkswagen, Microsoft, FedEx, S&P Global, Cisco, Deloitte, and Siemens, among dozens of other global enterprises. The archive has not yet been widely leaked. That window, Hudson Rock warned, will not remain open indefinitely. The critical information for enterprise security teams is not the size of the archive. It is the finding that Beaumont independently confirmed: for many of the organizations represented in the dataset, the stolen credentials are still live. The "40-minute window" that characterized early reporting on this breach — the time malicious packages were available on PyPI before being quarantined — describes the exposure period for the package registry. It does not describe the damage window. That window runs from March 24, 2026, when the malicious packages were first installed in corporate pipelines, until the day every affected organization rotates every credential those pipelines held. Five months later, that day has not arrived for a significant share of the 2,488 named domains. ### Why the Attack Window Did Not Close When PyPI Did The LiteLLM supply chain attack has a specific technical architecture that makes it harder to remediate than most credential thefts — and understanding it is the first s...

Security company CloudThe SEC now estimates that the attack on the open-source LiteLLM library could potentially affect more than 2500 organizations and approximately 434,000 CI/CD pipelines. This is not a typical attack on a single company. The hackers exploited the software supply chain, which allowed them to reach much further.  LiteLLM is an open-source tool used to work with various AI models and their APIs. Attackers according to CloudThe SEC first compromised the Trivy security tool and then used it to gain access to the LiteLLM build process, resulting in the release of malicious versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 to the PyPI repository.  ## You might be interested in [![Meta offers one billion Dollars to AI researchers in crazy poaching spree but they decline](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw== "Meta-offers-one-billion-Dollars-to-AI-researcher-in-crazy-poaching-spree-but-they-decline")](https://www.letemsvetemapplem.eu/en/2026/08/06/ai-od-mety-zautocila-na-system-jine-firmy-stalo-se-to-uz-potreti-behem-par-dnu/ "Meta's AI attacked another company's system. Once installed, it would automatically run when Python was started via a .pth file and attempt to extract sensitive information from the compromised environment. Attackers could have come across SSH keys, login credentials, etc. cloudto AWS, Google services Cloud and Azure, Kubernetes tokens, CI/CD secrets or API keys to AI services.  Interestingly, the malicious packages themselves were CloudThe SEC was only available for about 40 minutes. However, that doesn't mean that the problem was solved after they were removed. Once the malware had obtained the credentials, the attackers could use them for a long time afterwards. CloudThe SEC therefore warns that removing the compromised package alone does not resolve the incident.  And the range of companies potentially affected is truly impressive. Open Source AI.content: [![siteLogo](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/news_logo.svg)](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/) [Authorized Training Partner Updates (ATP)](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/?category=authorized-training-partner) [Affiliate Partner Program (APP)](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/?category=affiliate-partner-program) [Login](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/login/) [Sign Up](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/register/) ![](https://www.aicerts.ai/news/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/LOGO-DP-2-150x150.png) ###### AI CERTS 10 hours ago ## Meta Launches Muse Glimmer as Zuckerberg Doubles Down on Open AI Models and the Need for AI Training The development matters beyond the technology sector. As AI models become more accessible, businesses, developers and professionals will have more opportunities to experiment with AI directly. At the same time, this wider access creates a growing need for people who understand how to use these models effectively, responsibly and securely. AI training can help turn access to new technology into practical workplace skills. ## **Meta’s Muse Glimmer Signals a Shift Toward Accessible AI** Meta describes Muse Glimmer as a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model optimized for always-on local agent workflows. Its potential applications include local AI agents, function calling, coding and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation. The model is a distilled version of Meta’s Muse Spark 1.2 and is the first open model developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs, the company’s reorganized AI division. ![Meta Muse Glimmer open AI model driving demand for AI training and skills](https://aicertswpcdn.blob.core.windows.net/newsportal/2026/08/nano-banana-2_artistic_portrait_photography_of_Illustration_of_Meta_Muse_Glimmer_open_AI_model-0.jpg) Meta Muse Glimmer highlights the growing importance of AI training as open AI models become more accessible to businesses and professionals. Meta also plans to release the open weights for Muse Spark 1.2. Alongside the model announcements, Zuckerberg outlined his wider AI vision in a 14-page essay, arguing that the United States and its allies should lead the open-source AI ecosystem. The company’s latest move follows growing support from technology leaders for open models as a way to expand access to AI and encourage competition. For businesses, the important message is that AI capabilities are becoming easier to access and deploy. Organizations may increasingly have options beyond relying only on closed AI platforms. This can create opportunities for local applications, customized workflows and experimentation with AI tools that fit specific business needs. ## **More Accessible AI Creates a Skills Gap** Access to an AI model does not automatically mean an organization knows how to use it well. Employees need to understand how models work, where they can be applied and where human judgment remains necessary. This becomes even more important when AI is used for coding, research, customer service, analysis or automated workflows. The rise of open-weight models also introduces questions around data, security, model evaluation and responsible use. Zuckerberg’s comments specifically point to policy questions surrounding data use in training and model distillation. For businesses adopting these technologies, employees need enough AI knowledge to recognize these considerations rather than treating every model as a simple plug-and-play tool. This is where structured AI training becomes important. Training can help employees move from merely experimenting with AI to understanding how to apply it to real tasks. It can also help organizations build a common level of AI literacy across technical and non-technical teams. ## **The Opportunity for AI Trained Professionals** The Muse Glimmer launch points to several opportunities for professionals who build practical AI skills. Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [Cloud, Colocation & Connectivity](/news/cloud-colocation-connectivity) * 3 minRead # Zayo, Nvidia expand fiber capacity for AI infrastructure Zayo is building over 8,000 miles of long-haul fiber across emerging AI corridors with Nvidia as an anchor customer, addressing the growing demand for dedicated high-capacity connectivity. This expansion targets existing network constraints and the need for new physical routes to support distributed AI computing clusters and data centers. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 08:50 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Zayo is deploying over 8,000 miles of new long-haul fiber for AI corridors. * Nvidia is an anchor customer for Zayo's expanded fiber network. * The buildout addresses growing demand for dedicated connectivity for AI data centers. * Optical equipment constraints are impacting capacity upgrades on existing routes. [Zayo](/tag/zayo), a [digital infrastructure](/tag/digital+infrastructure) provider, is expanding its long-haul fiber network by over 8,000 miles across emerging artificial intelligence (AI) corridors, with [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) serving as an anchor customer. The Denver-based company plans to build six new long-haul routes and increase capacity in 10 high-demand markets, bringing its North American AI-focused network footprint to more than 15,000 route miles. This buildout aims to integrate networking into the core infrastructure required for AI, alongside power, data center capacity, and computing hardware. The expansion is critical as existing fiber routes, designed for legacy data center topologies, are encountering capacity limitations due to the geographical spread of AI factories and distributed computing clusters. ### Addressing Network Bottlenecks While some analysts, like Jimmy Yu, Vice President at Dell'Oro Group, suggest wide-area network bottlenecks from AI traffic are still in early stages, others, including Ron Westfall, Vice President at HyperFrame Research, indicate that existing routes are already nearing capacity limits. Westfall noted that as AI factories move into new markets to access available power, wide-area optical capacity is becoming a rate-limiting factor. Yu added that purpose-built routes with low latency and thousands of fiber pairs could become essential for connecting AI data centers, other facilities, and exchange points. Zayo's strategy is to build ahead of this anticipated demand, connecting areas where existing long-haul capacity is limited or non-existent, and expanding capacity on existing routes where demand is expected to surge. ### Optical Equipment Constraints The expansion efforts face near-term challenges from optical equipment availability. Yu highlighted that pump lasers used in amplifiers and coherent transponders are currently constrained, with product lead times from vendors like Ciena and Nokia extending beyond 12 months. This equipment scarcity can delay efforts to increase traffic capacity on existing fiber routes, even as new AI campuses create a separate need for entirely new physical routes. New fiber routes typically require over a year to build, sometimes approaching two years, a timeline similar to new data center construction. This synchronisation issue means that data centers could be completed and equipped with graphics processing units (GPUs) but lack the necessary connectivity to function as part of a larger distributed AI system, according to Yu. ### Strategic Network for AI Workloads Zayo CEO Steve Smith stated that AI is fundamentally reshaping network infrastructure requirements across the U.S. The compan...

This initiative, however, shifts the primary constraint for AI deployments from capital to power-ready sites and grid interconnection. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 09:10 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Nvidia partners with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR. * Over $500 billion in third-party capital targeted for AI infrastructure financing. * Initiative aims to lower Nvidia-based compute financing costs and shift GPU spending. * Easier capital does not resolve grid interconnection queues, transformer lead times, or permitting. * Power-ready sites and existing electrical infrastructure become more valuable due to financing shift. * $500 billion is a financing target, not committed spending, subject to definitive agreements. [Nvidia](/tag/nvidia) has partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish financing platforms designed to mobilise over $500 billion of third-party capital for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure over time. This initiative could reduce financing costs for Nvidia-based compute and move more graphics processing unit (GPU) spending off data center operators' balance sheets, according to Stephen Sopko, practice lead at HyperFrame Research. However, this capital injection does not address critical physical infrastructure constraints. It will not shorten [interconnection](/tag/interconnection) queues, accelerate the delivery of transformers and turbines, or resolve permitting issues, Sopko noted. "Easier capital shortens the distance to financial close," Sopko said. "It does nothing to the interconnect queue, transformer and turbine lead times, or permitting." ### Power-Ready Sites Gain Value This dynamic is expected to increase the value of power-ready sites, advanced interconnection positions, and existing electrical infrastructure, as financing becomes less of a bottleneck. Sopko views the financing push not merely as a demand story for AI compute but as Nvidia's signal for where it anticipates the next major constraint. The initiative could change the financing structure for AI compute, potentially lowering the cost of capital and moving more GPU spend off operators' balance sheets.Nvidia states that the new platforms will offer long-duration, usage-linked financing for [AI factories](/tag/ai+factories), providing AI labs, enterprises, and AI clouds with additional funding avenues for Nvidia-based infrastructure. This structure alters the financing model rather than the underlying cost of building the infrastructure itself. Sopko explained that treating compute as an underwritable asset with usage-linked revenue lowers the cost of capital and shifts GPU spending off the operator balance sheet. ### Residual Value Support Nvidia's residual-value support, capped at 25% of an individual opportunity and assessed project-by-project, offers lenders a mechanism to price GPU depreciation, which can otherwise be difficult to forecast. Infra & Chips.content: French Startup Kog Challenges GPU Inference Limits | The Tech Buzz [## the tech buzz](/) French Startup Kog Challenges GPU Inference Limits [AI](/articles)/[AI inference](/topics/ai-inference) # French Startup Kog Challenges GPU Inference Limits Kog claims GPUs aren't the bottleneck for agentic AI workflows everyone thinks they are by [The Tech Buzz](/authors/the-tech-buzz) PUBLISHED: Fri, Aug 14, 2026, 3:44 PM UTC| UPDATED: Fri, Aug 14, 2026, 4:20 PM UTC [Add as a preferred source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=techbuzz.ai) ![French Startup Kog Challenges GPU Inference Limits](/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,quality=85,format=auto,fit=cover/https://charming-card-d91ad3487b.media.strapiapp.com/large_file_f47a4bc98b.png) A French startup is taking aim at one of AI's accepted truths. Kog believes the industry has it wrong about GPUs being poorly suited for agentic workflows - the multi-step AI processes that power everything from coding assistants to autonomous research tools. While competitors race to build specialized chips, Kog is betting it can squeeze dramatically more inference performance out of existing GPU infrastructure by going deeper into the software stack. The AI infrastructure world has largely accepted a painful reality: GPUs, those workhorses of the generative AI boom, hit serious limitations when running agentic workflows. These multi-step processes - where AI models plan, execute, and iterate on complex tasks - create the kind of intermittent, unpredictable compute patterns that supposedly make GPUs inefficient compared to their performance on straightforward inference tasks. But [Kog](https://kog.ai), a startup emerging from France's growing AI ecosystem, isn't buying it. The company is challenging this accepted wisdom with a contrarian bet: the problem isn't the hardware, it's how we're using it. The timing matters. As enterprises rush to deploy agentic AI systems - think coding assistants that debug their own work or research tools that plan multi-stage investigations - infrastructure costs are becoming prohibitive. [Nvidia's](https://nvidia.com) H100 GPUs, the gold standard for AI workloads, remain in short supply and command premium prices. This crunch has sparked a wave of startups building specialized inference chips, from [Groq's](https://groq.com) language processing units to [Cerebras's](https://cerebras.net) wafer-scale engines. Kog is zigging while the industry zags. Rather than designing new silicon, the startup is diving deep into the software layer, rethinking how inference workloads get scheduled, batched, and executed on existing GPUs. The core insight: current inference frameworks treat agentic workflows like they're just really complicated single queries, when they actually need fundamentally different optimization strategies. The misconception about GPU performance stems from how agentic systems work. Traditional inference is straightforward - a user sends a prompt, the model processes it in one go, returns an answer. Agentic workflows are messier. The AI might generate code, run it, analyze the results, revise its approach, and iterate multiple times. Each step creates idle time as the system waits for external tools or processes intermediate results. Advertisement That's where conventional thinking says GPUs fail. These chips excel at massive parallel processing, but all that computational firepower sits idle during the waiting periods inherent to agentic tasks. It's like using a sports car for stop-and-go city traffic - technically possible, but seemingly wasteful. Kog's counterargument appears to focus on smarter orchestration. If you can better predict when those waiting periods happen, you can pack multiple agentic workflows onto the same GPU, swapping tasks in and out to keep the processors consistently fed with work. It's not unlike how modern operating systems handle multitasking, but optimized for the specific patterns of AI inference. This approach, if it works,...

Infra & Chips.content: [![datacenters logo](/_icons/logos/datacenters-logo-header.svg?mod=2)](/) * [AI & Compute Infrastructure](/news/ai-compute-infrastructure) * 3 minRead # Anthropic's IPO Signals Shift to Data Centre Ownership Anthropic, an artificial intelligence (AI) lab, is reportedly shifting its strategy from renting hyperscaler compute to building and owning its own data centre infrastructure. This strategic pivot, preceding a potential US listing, has implications for colocation operators, GPU cloud lenders, and power markets. * [ETDatacenters](/agency/88676092/ETDatacenters "ETDatacenters") * Published On Aug 14, 2026 at 09:00 AM IST * [![Google Preference icon](https://img.etb2bimg.com/files/cp/6e49a4e9b325074f01a6.png)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenters.economictimes.indiatimes.com "Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google") Select ETDatacenters as Preferred Choice on Google ## Highlights * Anthropic is shifting from renting hyperscaler compute to building and owning its own data centre infrastructure. * Apollo and Blackstone structured a $35 billion chip-backed SPV for Anthropic, with Fluidstack deploying capacity. * Anthropic pledged $50 billion for US computing infrastructure, building sites in Texas and New York. * Power supply and grid interconnection are emerging as critical bottlenecks for AI data centre expansion. [Anthropic](/tag/anthropic), a frontier artificial intelligence (AI) lab, is increasingly building and owning its own physical infrastructure rather than primarily relying on hyperscaler compute capacity, according to recent reports and financial filings. This strategic shift is emerging as a key detail ahead of the company's confidential US listing, which some reports suggest could value it between $965 billion and $2 trillion. Until recently, Anthropic's compute strategy involved renting capacity from Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and SpaceX. However, a significant change was observed in June when Apollo and [Blackstone](/tag/blackstone) structured a $35 billion chip-backed special purpose vehicle (SPV) for Anthropic. The initial gigawatt of capacity from this deal is being deployed through UK neocloud provider [Fluidstack](/tag/fluidstack), rather than Anthropic's established hyperscaler partners. This move highlights a preference for delivery certainty and custom-built facilities over existing balance sheet relationships. ### Infrastructure Investment Scale The shift is further underscored by Anthropic's pledge of $50 billion towards US computing infrastructure, with plans to build purpose-designed sites with Fluidstack in Texas and New York. This development is expected to create 800 permanent jobs and 2,400 construction jobs. Dario Amodei, Anthropic's chief executive, stated that this expenditure is necessary for infrastructure capable of supporting continued development at the frontier of AI. In addition to these investments, Anthropic has a $150 billion chip agreement with Google. The company also has an existing $11 billion Amazon Web Services (AWS) campus in Indiana and multi-cloud access to Google tensor processing units (TPUs) and Microsoft Azure. The deployment is the first announced commercial capacity commitment in the South Wales AI Growth Zone, and the infrastructure will support AI training, inference, agentic AI and enterprise workloads for businesses, researchers, startups and public sector organizations. According to a [press release](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260813253918/en/Vantage-Data-Centers-and-Nebius-Expand-UK-AI-Infrastructure-with-First-Deployment-in-South-Wales-AI-Growth-Zone), Vantage’s CWL1 campus has operated since 2010, and is one of Europe’s largest data center campuses. The company plans to deliver more than 1GW of AI-ready capacity across Newport, Bridgend, and Bro Tathan, as part of a multi-billion-pound investment in South Wales. The CWL1 campus’s electricity consumption is matched with 100 percent certified renewable energy. Its newer facilities use closed-loop cooling systems designed to reduce operational water consumption, alongside air-cooled chillers and free cooling when conditions allow. Readers will recall that [Nebius](https://w.media/nebius-to-invest-1-7-billion-in-uk-for-ai-infrastructure-expansion/) had announced plans to invest approximately £1.7 billion (US$ 2.3 billion) in new AI infrastructure by building three new facilities in the UK with a combined capacity of 65 MW by 2027. Its UK infrastructure plans use NVIDIA’s DSX AI factory reference design and are intended to support the UK government’s AI Opportunities Action Plan. David Howson, President, EMEA, Vantage Data Centers, said, “This is an important milestone for South Wales and for the UK’s AI infrastructure ambitions, Nebius is scaling AI cloud infrastructure in the UK at a time when demand for domestic compute capacity continues to accelerate.
